text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.08% today, but this modest gain masks a brutal two-week decline of 9.12% that reflects the core problem facing refiners right now: refining margins are shrinking. Even though crude oil prices spiked Wednesday on geopolitical tensions (U.S. preparing possible Iran strikes), gasoline prices fell simultaneously—a squeeze that cuts directly into refiner profits. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with ample fuel inventories (gasoline up, diesel stable), so there's no supply tightness to support margins, and the Trump administration's moves to allow more Russian diesel into the market add further downward pressure.

The stock's micro-bounce today likely reflects the oil price rally on Middle East conflict fears, but that tailwind is offset by the structural headwind: lower margins mean lower earnings for refiners regardless of crude prices. The week's 34-point drop through October 27 was the real story, driven by the gasoline-price collapse signaling that refining economics have deteriorated meaningfully.
